newsitem.title: UK: Whessoe backs Navia in endorsement switch.
newsitem.headline: Whessoe backs Navia in endorsement switch.

text.p: Britain's Whessoe Plc on Friday withdrew its recommendation of a bid by Siebe Plc and said it would back a rival offer from Navia and Endress+Hauser.
The move came after British engineering giant Siebe said on Thursday it would not increase its 155 pence per share bid for the instruments and controls company.
Whessoe said Navia and Endress+Hauser's joint 175 pence per share cash bid was about 12.9 percent higher than Siebe's cash offer and 16.6 percent higher than that company's share alternative.
The company said the offer by Norway's Navia and Swiss-based Endress+Hauser valued it at about 52.6 million pounds ($85.7 million), compared to Siebe's estimated 46.6 million pound bid.

"Accordingly, the directors of Whessoe withdraw their recommendation of Siebe's offer and will unanimously recommend shareholders to accept the offer of Navia and Endress+Hauser," Whessoe said in a statement.
Earlier this week, Navia and Endress said they had already bought about 3.14 million Whessoe shares, or about 10.6 percent of its capital.
Whessoe's shares slid 1.5 pence to 173.5, while Siebe's shares slipped 1.0 pence to 967.5 at 1300 GMT. ($ = 0.614 British Pounds)
